nodes.natural_language: Square the rewritten condition and obtain the quadratic in p whose discriminant forces s>=4.
nodes.statement: Squaring \(\sqrt{p}\sqrt{s^2-4p}=s\) produces the quadratic equation 4p^2 - s^2 p + s^2 =0; non-negative discriminant requires s^2(s^2-16)>=0, hence s>=4 (with equality possible when the root p lies in (0,s^2/4)).

The quadratic in p has real roots if and only if s^{2}(s^{2}-16)\ge0, hence s\ge4 (and the resulting p is positive and at most s^{2}/4).

nodes.natural_language: The inequality (t^{2}+1)^{2}\ge4t(t^{2}-1) rearranges to (t^{2}-2t-1)^{2}\ge0, which holds for all t>1.

nodes.natural_language: The quadratic in p has positive roots satisfying the interval condition precisely when s>=4.
nodes.statement: The quadratic in \(p\) has positive roots \(p=[s^2\pm s\sqrt{s^2-16}]/8\) satisfying \(0<p\le s^2/4\) precisely when \(s\ge4\), so the given relation forces \(s\ge4\).
